2096-a-smaller-history-of-greece-from-th.title: from the earliest times to the Roman conquest.
2096-a-smaller-history-of-greece-from-th.creator: William Smith,  D.C.L., Ll.D.
2096-a-smaller-history-of-greece-from-th.description: A book by William Smith,  D.C.L., Ll.D.. Greece is the southern portion of a great peninsula of Europe, washed on three sides by the Mediterranean Sea. It is bounded on the north by the Cambunian mountains, which separate it from Macedonia. It extends from the fortieth degree of latitude to the thirty-sixth, its greatest length being not more than 250 English miles, and its greatest breadth only 180.

arxiv-2202-07793.title: Heuristic computation of exact treewidth
arxiv-2202-07793.creator: Hisao Tamaki
arxiv-2202-07793.description: Abstract We are interested in computing the treewidth tw ( G ) {\mathop{\rm tw}}(G) of a given graph G G . Our approach is to design heuristic algorithms for computing a sequence of improving upper bounds and a sequence of improving lower bounds, which would hopefully converge to tw ( G ) {\mathop{\rm tw}}(G) from both sides.

arxiv-2203-01703.title: Capturing Shape Information with Multi-Scale Topological Loss Terms for 3D Reconstruction
arxiv-2203-01703.creator: Dominik J. E. Waibel, Scott Atwell, Matthias Meier, Carsten Marr, Bastian Rieck
arxiv-2203-01703.description: Abstract Reconstructing 3D objects from 2D images is both challenging for our brains and machine learning algorithms. To support this spatial reasoning task, contextual information about the overall shape of an object is critical. However, such information is not captured by established loss terms (e.g. Dice loss).

arxiv-2308-12110.title: Constrained Stein Variational Trajectory Optimization
arxiv-2308-12110.creator: Thomas Power, Dmitry Berenson
arxiv-2308-12110.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Thomas Power, Dmitry Berenson. We present Constrained Stein Variational Trajectory Optimization (CSVTO), an algorithm for performing trajectory optimization with constraints on a set of trajectories in parallel. We frame constrained trajectory optimization as a novel form of constrained functional minimization over trajectory distributions, which avoids treating the constraints as a penalty in the objective and allows us to generate diverse sets of constraint-satisfying trajectories.

arxiv-2310-19853.title: Soft modes in hot QCD matter
arxiv-2310-19853.creator: Jens Braun, Yong-rui Chen, Wei-jie Fu, Fei Gao, Chuang Huang, Friederike Ihssen, Jan M. Pawlowski, Fabian Rennecke, Franz R. Sattler, Yang-yang Tan, Rui Wen, Shi Yin
arxiv-2310-19853.description: Abstract The chiral crossover of QCD at finite temperature and vanishing baryon density turns into a second order phase transition if lighter than physical quark masses are considered. If this transition occurs sufficiently close to the physical point, its universal critical behaviour would largely control the physics of the QCD phase transition.

arxiv-2405-03688.title: Large Language Models Reveal Information Operation Goals, Tactics, and Narrative Frames
arxiv-2405-03688.creator: Keith Burghardt Kai Chen Kristina Lerman
arxiv-2405-03688.description: Abstract Adversarial information operations can destabilize societies by undermining fair elections, manipulating public opinions on policies, and promoting scams. Despite their widespread occurrence and potential impacts, our understanding of influence campaigns is limited by manual analysis of messages and subjective interpretation of their observable behavior.

arxiv-2409-01439.title: Computing virtual dark-field X-ray microscopy images of complex discrete dislocation structures from large-scale molecular dynamics simulations
arxiv-2409-01439.creator: Yifan, Nicolas, Dayeeta, Kento, Sara J, Robert E
arxiv-2409-01439.description: Abstract Dark-field X-ray Microscopy (DFXM) is a novel diffraction-based imaging technique that non-destructively maps the local deformation from crystalline defects in bulk materials. While studies have demonstrated that DFXM can spatially map 3D defect geometries, it is still challenging to interpret DFXM images of the high dislocation density systems relevant to macroscopic crystal plasticity.

arxiv-2509-16148.title: On Tent Spaces for the Gaussian Measure
arxiv-2509-16148.creator: Liliana Forzani, Roberto Scotto, Wilfredo Urbina
arxiv-2509-16148.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Liliana Forzani, Roberto Scotto, Wilfredo Urbina. Following the scheme of tent spaces in classical harmonic analysis developed by R. In [ 8 ] , part of this theory (an atomic decomposition) is developed for a specific tent space where functions are defined just in a proper subset of ℝ + n + 1 , \mathbb{R}^{n+1}_{+}, and without the use of an area function.

arxiv-2511-16521.title: YOWO: You Only Walk Once to Jointly Map An Indoor Scene and Register Ceiling-mounted Cameras
arxiv-2511-16521.creator: Fan Yang, Sosuke Yamao, Ikuo Kusajima, Atsunori Moteki, Shoichi Masui, Shan Jiang
arxiv-2511-16521.description: Abstract Using ceiling-mounted cameras (CMCs) for indoor visual capturing opens up a wide range of applications. However, registering CMCs to the target scene layout presents a challenging task. While manual registration with specialized tools is inefficient and costly, automatic registration with visual localization may yield poor results when visual ambiguity exists.

pmc-11443958.creator: Edward D Shin, Eugene Fan
pmc-11443958.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundAortic stenosis (AS) is the most commonly acquired valvular pathology in the western world. Aortic stenosis severity is typically evaluated with Doppler echocardiography. Evaluation of aortic gradients using standard Doppler echocardiography from the apical window may underestimate the true gradient due to misalignment of blood flow to the ultrasound beam and is often better evaluated from other imaging windows using a non-imaging continuous wave Doppler (NI-CWD) probe.
